items.readable_text:
Content:
The volume of a shape is the amount of [MATH: 3]-dimensional space inside it. We can calculate the volume of a rectangular prism with the following formula:
[MATH: V = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height}]

Content:
Let's use this to calculate the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/0f8dfac8c54f990fac9201168ac41b51]

Content:
This rectangular prism has a length of [MATH: 2\,\text{km}], a width of [MATH: \dfrac{3}{2} \,\text{km}], and a height of [MATH: \dfrac{5}{2}\,\text{km}.]

Content:
So, the volume of the rectangular prism is:
[MATH: V|= length × width × height; = 2 × (3)/(2) × (5)/(2); = (2 × 3 × 5)/(1 × 2 × 2); = (30)/(4)]

Content:
We can simplify the fraction above by dividing the numerator and denominator by [MATH: 2\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{30 \div 2}{4 \div 2}= \dfrac{15}{2}]

Content:
Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{15}{2} = 7 \, \textrm{R} \, 1 = 7 \, \dfrac{1}{2}]

Content:
Therefore, the volume is [MATH: 7 \, \dfrac{1}{2}\,\text{km}^3.]

So, the volume of the rectangular prism is: [MATH: V|= length × width × height; = 2 × (3)/(4) × (2)/(3); = (2)/(1) × (3)/(4) × (2)/(3); = (2 × 3 × 2)/(1 × 4 × 3); = (12)/(12)]

We now simplify the above fraction by dividing the numerator and denominator by [MATH: 12\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \dfrac{12 \div 12}{12 \div 12}= \dfrac{1}{1} = 1]

Therefore, the volume of the rectangular prism is [MATH: 1 \,\text{cm}^3.]

sections.normalized_html:
The rectangular prism has a length of [MATH: 3 \, \text{in}], a width of [MATH: 1\,\dfrac{1}{3} \,\text{in}], and a height of [MATH: 2\,\text{in}.]

So, the volume of the rectangular prism is: [MATH: V|= length × width × height; = 3 × 1(1)/(3) × 2]

We write [MATH: 1 \, \dfrac{1}{3}] as an improper fraction:

[MATH: 1 \, \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{(1 \times 3) + 1}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}]

Now, we can multiply the numbers:

[MATH: V|= 3 × (4)/(3) × 2; = (3 × 4 × 2)/(3); = (24)/(3); = 8]

Therefore, the volume is [MATH: 8 \,\text{in}^3.]

items.readable_text:
Content:
We can also calculate the volume of a rectangular prism if we know the height and the area of the base. All we have to do is multiply these quantities together:
[MATH: V = \text{base} \times \text{height}]

Content:
Let's apply this formula to find the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/252349f874fb661528fb6bc2c6e6f0ee]

Content:
For this rectangular prism, the area of the base is [MATH: 8 \, \text{cm}^2] and the height is [MATH: \dfrac{3}{4} \, \text{cm}.]

Content:
So, the volume of the rectangular prism is:
[MATH: V|= base × height; = 8 × (3)/(4); = (8 × 3)/(4); = (24)/(4); = 6]

Content:
Therefore, the volume is [MATH: 6 \, \text{cm}^3.]

Content:
Note: Where does this formula come from? The key is to realize that the area of the base of a rectangular prism is equal to the length multiplied by the width:

Content:
[MATH: \text{base} = \text{length} \times \text{width}]

Content:
Looking at the original formula for calculating the volume of a rectangular prism, we have:
[MATH: V|= length × width × height; = (length × width) × height; = base × height]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The volume of a shape is the amount of [MATH: 3]-dimensional space inside it. We can calculate the volume of a rectangular prism with the following formula:
[MATH: V = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height}]

Content:
Let's use this to calculate the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/0f8dfac8c54f990fac9201168ac41b51]

Content:
This rectangular prism has a length of [MATH: 2\,\text{km}], a width of [MATH: \dfrac{3}{2} \,\text{km}], and a height of [MATH: \dfrac{5}{2}\,\text{km}.]

Content:
So, the volume of the rectangular prism is:
[MATH: V|= length × width × height; = 2 × (3)/(2) × (5)/(2); = (2 × 3 × 5)/(1 × 2 × 2); = (30)/(4)]

Content:
We can simplify the fraction above by dividing the numerator and denominator by [MATH: 2\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{30 \div 2}{4 \div 2}= \dfrac{15}{2}]

Content:
Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{15}{2} = 7 \, \textrm{R} \, 1 = 7 \, \dfrac{1}{2}]

Content:
Therefore, the volume is [MATH: 7 \, \dfrac{1}{2}\,\text{km}^3.]

---

Item 2 — Example: Calculating the Volume of a Rectangular Prism

Example Prompt:
What is the volume of the rectangular prism shown below?

[IMG: /graphics/4d8a7338f61c3708dfd6f6bee57432c3]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The rectangular prism has a length of [MATH: 2\,\text{cm}], a width of [MATH: \dfrac{3}{4}\,\text{cm}], and a height of [MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}\,\text{cm}.]

So, the volume of the rectangular prism is:
[MATH: V|= length × width × height; = 2 × (3)/(4) × (2)/(3); = (2)/(1) × (3)/(4) × (2)/(3); = (2 × 3 × 2)/(1 × 4 × 3); = (12)/(12)]

We now simplify the above fraction by dividing the numerator and denominator by [MATH: 12\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \dfrac{12 \div 12}{12 \div 12}= \dfrac{1}{1} = 1]

Therefore, the volume of the rectangular prism is [MATH: 1 \,\text{cm}^3.]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Volumes of Rectangular Prisms Given the Height and Base Area

Content:
We can also calculate the volume of a rectangular prism if we know the height and the area of the base. All we have to do is multiply these quantities together:
[MATH: V = \text{base} \times \text{height}]

Content:
Let's apply this formula to find the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/252349f874fb661528fb6bc2c6e6f0ee]

Content:
For this rectangular prism, the area of the base is [MATH: 8 \, \text{cm}^2] and the height is [MATH: \dfrac{3}{4} \, \text{cm}.]

Content:
So, the volume of the rectangular prism is:
[MATH: V|= base × height; = 8 × (3)/(4); = (8 × 3)/(4); = (24)/(4); = 6]

Content:
Therefore, the volume is [MATH: 6 \, \text{cm}^3.]

Content:
Note: Where does this formula come from? The key is to realize that the area of the base of a rectangular prism is equal to the length multiplied by the width:

Content:
[MATH: \text{base} = \text{length} \times \text{width}]

Content:
Looking at the original formula for calculating the volume of a rectangular prism, we have:
[MATH: V|= length × width × height; = (length × width) × height; = base × height]
